title: EmbeddingGemma 2: an open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
key_facts: Google launched EmbeddingGemma 2, an embedding model that maps text, code, images, video and audio into one shared space.
It is built on the Gemma 4 architecture, has 740 million parameters and is released under the Apache 2.0 licence.
The first EmbeddingGemma has had more than 20 million downloads, Google says.
On the MTEB Code test its score rose from 68.76 to 78.68, a 9.92-point gain.
Google says it beats some specialist models more than twice its size on image, video, document and audio tasks.
Embeddings can be generated on the device, which Google says helps privacy and works offline.
quote_evidence: Today, we’re launching EmbeddingGemma 2, expanding beyond text to unify code, images, video, and audio in a shared embedding space.
EmbeddingGemma 2 matches the strong multilingual text performance of EmbeddingGemma while delivering a significant 9.92-point improvement on code performance (in MTEB Code, from 68.76 to 78.68).
why_it_matters_hint: Lets developers build search over photos, video, audio and code that runs on a phone or laptop without sending data to a server.
notes: Read the Google blog post (company announcement); performance claims are Google's own.
